entry.title: Social Summary: September 24, 2026
entry.summary:
Lead story — Bot Screen / Live Desktop Passthrough launch: The week was dominated by the coordinated launch of Bot Screen for Hermes Desktop. @NousResearch's official announcement (streaming any bot's screen/session live) and @Teknium's launch post on interactive visual passthrough to the agent's machine pulled the section's biggest engagement by far. An official @tonbistudio walkthrough with docs link, plus Teknium amplifying the same guide video, gave newcomers an immediate on-ramp. Community sentiment was emphatically positive — "Finallllly!" and "Much needed!" (204 likes, 20k views) suggest this was one of the most-requested Hermes capabilities to date.

Ecosystem builds in the open — oh-my-hermes & Jev tooling: @rlaope had a strong week: open-sourcing jeval (evaluation + visual result extraction for Jev) and shipping OMH+ updates to oh-my-hermes with Jev skills, plugins and aliases, model routing, and JEV-powered workflows — positioning OMH as the all-in-one plugin for AI-native Hermes Agent users. A healthy signal of third-party tooling maturing around the agent.

Official tips & responsive support: @NousResearch highlighted a practical flex — Hermes works over iMessage with any model of your choosing. @Teknium shipped a quick fix in response to user feedback and set clear bug-report etiquette in a cache dispute (reproducible path or it didn't happen), while also clarifying provenance in a multi-party thread: the discussed artifact was built by the Nous/Hermes team, not Anthropic.

Community pulse: Short-but-warm endorsements ("Impressive!", "This is the way") and celebratory emoji replies reinforce broadly positive sentiment centered on the launch. Curated out: duplicate jeval/OMH link drops, emoji-only replies, engagement-bait, and one off-topic take on Opus 5.5 vs Claude Code that falls outside Hermes scope.
